newsitem.title: CHINA: HSBC Holdings seen posting healthy interim net.
newsitem.headline: HSBC Holdings seen posting healthy interim net.

text.p: HSBC Holdings Plc is expected to post healthy earnings growth for the first half of 1997 but some analysts said the results may not justify the torrid rise in its stock, which has smashed record after record.
"The results will be reasonably strong across the board," ING Barings senior investment analyst Peter Redhead said on Thursday. "The thing is whether the price justifies the growth."
HSBC is due to release its interim results on August 4.
Analysts forecast net profit growth of between six and 20 percent for the first six months of the year compared with interim net profit of HK$18.74 billion (US$2.42 billion) in 1996.
HSBC shares have risen 69 percent this year to close at an all-time high of HK$279.00 on Thursday.
"People are anticipating good earnings and the bank has indicated that it is ahead of expectations," said Roy Ramos, regional banking analyst at Goldman Sachs.
HSBC Holdings chairman William Purves said in May the banking giant's performance so far this year was ahead of plan.
"There has been a resurgence in loan growth in Hong Kong and the benign interest rate environment in the U.S. and the U.K. is a very conducive environment for the bank," said Ramos.
Alex Wong, banking analyst at Dharmala Securities, expected net profit growth of about 20 percent, with Hong Kong and the U.K. the main drivers.
Hong Kong accounts for about 40 percent of HSBC's earnings and the U.K. accounts for around 30 percent.
"Mortgage lending was still very good in Hong Kong during the first half and interest rates are stable," said Wong.
While mortgage competition has been fierce in Hong Kong, the booming property market should provide firm loan growth.
Keith Irving, banking analyst at Merrill Lynch, said he expected HSBC unit Hang Seng Bank Ltd to show 16 percent loan growth for the full year.
"Within Hong Kong, they have the benefit of coming from a very strong position," he said.
In the U.K., Irving saw loan growth at eight percent for the full year for unit Midland Bank Plc. "It is not very impressive by Hong Kong standards but it is pretty good by U.K. standards."

Irving said the consolidation of First Federal Savings and Loan Association of Rochester, New York, would also make a positive contribution. Marine Midland Bank, a unit of HSBC Americas Inc, completed the acquisition in March.
But Thomas Monaco, banking analyst at Bear Stearns, said he expected net profit growth of only six percent, citing a slowdown in loan growth in Hong Kong and margin compression.
Redhead saw a stable net interest margin due to the globalisation of HSBC. "Because HSBC is so huge it takes a lot of movement to move away from the 2.9 percent average level."
But Redhead said HSBC would "struggle to have very, very good results", predicting net profit growth in the low teens.
"Year-on-year comparisons will be difficult since last year they had some asset sales," he said.
First half 1996 profit from fixed asset and investment disposals totalled HK$3.1 billion.
"I think the share price rise is getting to a questionable point," said Redhead. "The results need to justify the price."
Analysts said HSBC shares had benefited from a re-rating of the banking sector in London.
"It has been the prime beneficiary of a flight to quality that you have seen in the region," said Ramos.
HSBC shares had also picked up some of the flow of money out of Thailand, the Philippines and Malaysia into Hong Kong, analysts said.
Irving said some investors may be disappointed with bottom line earnings.

"Reported earnings we don't think are going to look that impressive but operating profit growth should be very good," he said. "We have seen in the past that investors in Hong Kong can react to reported earnings."
